stem.en: A bar magnet is brought close to a compass. The magnet and the compass needle exert equal and opposite forces on each other. Why does only the needle move?

text.en: The needle is light and free to turn, while the magnet is much heavier and is held in your hand.

feedback.en: Right. The same force gives the light, free needle a large effect and the heavy, held magnet almost none.

text.en: The magnet exerts a larger force on the needle.

feedback.en: By the third law, the two forces are equal.

text.en: The needle exerts no force on the magnet.

feedback.en: Forces come in pairs. The needle pulls on the magnet too.

explanation.en: The forces are equal and opposite. The needle is light and turns freely on its pin, so the force turns it. The magnet is heavier and is held, so the equal force on it has no effect we can see.

hints.en: Compare the fruit and the Earth.
